narrative.overview: Kemudi is the helm of a delivery project. The sidebar is the wheelhouse: deep sea ink in both themes, with a single brass marker showing where you are. Everything to its right is the chart table, a quiet, cool work surface where the data (stories, sprints, statuses, people) does the talking.
keyCharacteristics: Deep-ink sidebar (the helm) in light and dark themes alike; the work surface switches.
Brass marks you: your place, your focus, your watches and unread notifications.
Cool blue-grey neutrals with a slight 250° hue; no warm greys.
Flat surfaces separated by hairlines, with a light shadow only on raised, movable or floating things.
Compact, scannable rows; status colors come from each project's own configuration.

rules.name: The Brass Means You Rule
rules.body: Brass marks you: where you are and what is yours (watching, voted, unread). Never decoration, status or layout fill; the dark theme primary button is the one sanctioned fill.

rules.name: The Meaning-Only Color Rule
rules.body: Outside the helm, color carries state: a status, a type, success or danger.

rules.name: The Two Sizes Rule
rules.body: Working UI lives at 14px and 12px; size steps above that are for page and section titles only.

rules.name: The Lift Means Movable Rule
rules.body: A shadow larger than xs says this floats or can be moved. Static containers stay flat with a hairline.

dos: Do keep the sidebar Helm Ink in both themes and mark the active item with the 3px Brass bar.
Do get text sizes from the 14px / 12px pair and build hierarchy with weight and Slate Muted.
Do let buttons, tabs, pills and table headers grow with their label; Indonesian strings run 20–40% longer.
donts: Don't use Brass for decoration, status or anything that isn't about the viewer.
Don't give static containers a drop shadow; shadows mean floating or movable.
Don't truncate action labels or fix button widths to fit English text.
